utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Djozo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djozo. I wonder if we can pick up where we left off yesterday when we were discussing the shelling of Dzenetica Cikme Street in Sarajevo. Do you remember where we left off yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we see please then 65 ter number 23066, which is an official report dated 26 May 1995, from the Stari Grad Public Security Station in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, have you seen this document in preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the official report done after on-site investigation was conducted concerning the shelling incident injuring children and people in Dzenetica Cikme Street. When the police station Stari Grad was informed that a shell exploded in that street, that some children were killed and wounded, an investigation team was formed, but it was only the next day that it managed to go out and investigate. The shelling took place on the 25th of June, 1995, in the evening, around 7.00 p.m., and an investigating judge of the High Court in Sarajevo was also informed, but he did not come to the scene. It was Judge Ibrahim Hadzic that came to the scene, and an official team from the CSB Sarajevo was formed. The duty officer for on-site investigation at the police station Stari Grad was there, a duty officer from the anti-sabotage unit of the KBZ BH -- sorry, KDZ, which is anti-sabotage unit, and a scenes of crime officer also from the CSB Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, your name is not mentioned in this document, is it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My name is not mentioned here for the simple reason that every day one person is assigned to be the duty officer for on-site investigations, and it so happened that these children were killed in the evening of one day and the on-site investigation was to be conducted the next day. Police officers from Stari Grad secured the site, and the next morning, upon the orders of my supervisor, I went with a couple of colleagues to help out in that on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, was this report made available to you prior to your giving testimony in the Perisic case?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I'm not sure whether I saw it then.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Perhaps you could assist us with respect to the date of the incident. You noted at paragraph 25 of your written evidence that to your knowledge, this incident took place about a month before Markale II, and you see in the document in your language in front of you the document itself is dated 26 May 1995, but it refers to an incident that took place on 25 June 1995. Could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the area held by the VRS, thousands of shells fell upon Stari Grad. One cannot remember when that was, what shells those were, what was going on. In the area of Dzenetica Cikme Street and part of Drvarksa Street covered by the police station Centar Bjelave, shellings were almost a daily occurrence, so we could not keep a record of that kind, when the shells were falling, whether there were some at that landed before and after, at what time. So that after all this time especially you can't be sure when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, given that the date on this document on the top left-hand corner of 26 May 1995 appears in that document only once, do you think that might have been a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such typographical errors should not be possible. It shouldn't be a typo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first line of the main report says it was created on 26th of June. Do you see that, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that. It's possible that in the left-hand top corner in the heading a typo was made, because in the body of the text they continued to refer to the 25th and the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I'd like to tender this report as the next Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a report as regards unscheduled shelling incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It is indeed, Your Honour, and I should underline that this evidence is not being led for the specific proof of this incident. This evidence, the evidence about this incident, is being led in relation to a scheduled incident, Markale II, on 28 August 1995, and it's part of the Prosecution's case that this evidence -- well, in fact this evidence corroborates and supports Mr. Djozo's evidence that the marketplace incident was a deliberate attack by Bosnian Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think if I tried to do something like this you wouldn't let me get away with it. This witness was neither an active participant nor is this incident scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to respond, Ms. Edgerton, before we deliberate?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, just, in fact, he was a participant. He's already given evidence that he attended the scene the next day and took part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's relevant. We don't see any problem admitting it. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1987, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo, in your written evidence at paragraphs 27 to 34, you referred to another incident which you described as being two or three days before or after the one we've just spoken about where three 120-millimetre shells fell in one line from the same direction of fire within the space of half an hour from each other, then a fourth 120-millimetre shell fell in the same neighbourhood coming from the same direction. And you noted at paragraph 33 that these shells fell within 100 metres from each other, creeping closer to the marketplace -- with the first three creeping closer to the marketplace with every shot. Do you remember that from your written evidence?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know very well how it all unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, then perhaps we could have 65 ter number 23002, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, do you recognise this document that appears on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the document, because I drew this.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what's depicted in this document then.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This drawing shows the place where shells landed and exploded after being fired from the area of Lukavica, Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does this refer to the incident we've just talked about where in your written evidence you said three 120-millimetre shells fell in one line from the same direction of fire within the space of half an hour?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first shell landed in Skenderija Street, now renamed Hamdije Kresevljakovica, in the compound of the public transportation company. There were some people killed and some wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, could you, before you go much further, do, as you did yesterday, and with the assistance of my colleague and the electronic marker in front of you indicate where to your recollection the first shell fell. And perhaps you could put a circle around the marking of where the first shell fell?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first shell fell in Skenderija Street, that is to say, Hamdije Kresevljakovica, and that's here. In this spot where the shell landed, people were wounded and killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we ask him to put number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, please. Marking a red circle at the bottom middle of the page, could you just write the number 1 beside that, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could you tell us how the rest of the incident unfolded. Where was the second shell?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next shell fell in the formerly JNA street, now Sarajevo Defenders Street, just next door to the Stari Grad town hall or municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Marking a further red circle with the number 2 beside it.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the third shell?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third shell fell in the street formerly known as Marsala Tita, now known as Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, and again there were dead and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you said then a fourth 120-millimetre shell fell in the same neighbourhood coming from the same direction, and where was that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth shell landed close to the faculty of economics, former Vase Miskina Street. It fell on the roof on the faculty of economics.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does this sketch that you've marked - oh, pardon me - indicating the location of the third and fourth shells with red circles and the numbers 3 and 4 beside them. Now, does this sketch you've drawn indicate the location of the shelling of Markale II on 28 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Markale II is marked, and it's roughly 50 metres, at any rate, less than 100 metres away in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street. That's the building of the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Fifty to 100 metres away from what?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building of the market is less than 100 metres away from shell number three, and the same distance from shell number four, not more than 100 metres away. Between 50 and 70 metres max.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1988, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we now go through a similar exercise to what we did yesterday and look at P1982, which is a map, Mr. Djozo, that you marked yesterday relating -- a sketch that you had made to the map itself, and I'd like you to go through the same exercise, please. P1982 is on the screen. Do you remember this map from yesterday, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, my colleague's going to assist you by making sure that you work in another colour, and what I'd like you to do is, as you did yesterday, mark the -- so you can orient all of us, mark the area indicated in the sketch we've just had on the screen in front of us, P1988.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first shell landed close to the Drvenija bridge in Skenderija Street, nowadays Hamdije Kresevljakovica Street, around here. The second one fell in Sarajevo Defenders Street close to the Stari Grad municipality building. The next one close to the faculty of economics. It fell actually on the roof of that building. Facing the faculty of economics. And the fourth one fell in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street. It hit a residential building where the ground floor was occupied by the Konzum company, and the upper floors were apartments.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to mark the blue dots you've placed on this map with numbers beside them indicating one for the first shell, two for the second, three for the third, and fourth for the last.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could this be the next Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1989, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we withdraw this map, to remind ourselves of the overall marking, the red one in Stari Grad refers to the location of the Stari Grad police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd invite the witness to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's marked as Stari Grad police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the red markings hidden behind the green markings refers to the location of Markale.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And green markings refers to what, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Petrarkina Street, Dzenetica Cikme Street, and Markale. I'm sorry, I didn't do this very well. I didn't mark explosion number three very well because it's even closer to Markale than I marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to erase number 3 and mark it again. Could you wait a minute, and the usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where I had marked number 3 is already Lugavina Street, Romanijska Street is below, Petrarkina and Dzenetica Cikme descend towards Mula Mustafe Baseskije. That would be number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we keep the previous version where the number 3 is differently marked? It was not kept. Thank you. Very well. This will be kept. Yes, Ms. Edgerton. This has been admitted as P1989 already.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. Could we turn, then, still on the subject of the incidents at this location, could we turn then to 65 ter 22999, an official report compiled following an on-site investigation on the occasion of the shelling of the city on 1 July 1995. Thank you. Mr. Djozo, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official report written concerning the shelling of central Sarajevo on the 1st of July. The shelling of Sarajevo, especially Stari Grad centre and Novo Sarajevo, were being targeted by heavy shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could go over, please, to page 2 in both versions of the document, paragraph 5 of the English, and paragraph 4, as I recall, in the B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see mention of your --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you make the B/C/S version a little bit clearer somehow. A little bit larger, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see mention of your name in paragraph 4 of the B/C/S version, Mr. Djozo? And sorry, my colleague, his name is actually a little bit cut off and it might be hard for him to see it in the version in his own language. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, immediately below your name appear reports of two separate shelling incidents. Do these refer in any way to the incidents we've just been discussing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is related to that investigation, those incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: In what capacity did you attend the scene?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the investigation team was formed, because the shelling was in the central areas of Sarajevo, ranging from Stari Grad to Novi Grad, the team had to go to each of the police stations, each of the places where the shelling was recorded. Since the shelling was quite fierce, as they were leaving the CSB building, they were progressing through the different investigations. In the Stari Grad area, where I was on duty that day, I waited for the investigation team in the Hamdije Kresevljakovica Street in Skenderija and I was waiting for them to investigate the shell that landed in Skenderija Street, because this was covered by the Stari Grad and the Centar police stations and the duty officer from the crime department had to be present from the Centar police station. Then we went to the Stari Grad area after that investigation was completed where I joined the investigation team. After that, together with the others, we came to the Branilaca Grada Street, the former JNA street, which was part of the Stari Grad municipality. This shell mostly wounded people. I didn't have information that anybody was killed. We finished that investigation, and after that we went to Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street where we also carried out an investigation. There were many dead, also many wounded people there. After that, the investigation team went to Novi Grad. The shell that landed across the street from the faculty of economics, hitting the roof, did not seem to wound or kill anyone. At least we didn't have such information. And since the shelling continued, the investigation team continued, and all we did was to document the fact that the shell landed on that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask that this be the next Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The relevance goes to the same issue as raised in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P1990, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Djozo, finally at paragraph 35 of your written evidence you said, and I'll quote: "My view regarding these and other shellings, which was shared by others at the police station, is that the fire was adjusted until they reached the very crowded Markale to cause a big number of casualties." And what would I like to ask you is when you referred in your written evidence to these and other shellings, what other shellings were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the aggression on Bosnia and Herzegovina from the very beginning of the shelling, all the shells were directed to areas where usually there were people gathering, where there were more people. We know that in Vase Miskina street at the very beginning of the war a lot of people were killed. All the shells were directed in such areas. The Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street was a street that most of Sarajevo's citizens used. It was visibly shielded from view from Trebevic, so all the citizens moved along that street. The only place where they could gather, where they could exchange goods and buy food for themselves, to exchange cigarettes for food, was Markale, and that is mostly where they stayed for a brief period of time to exchange the goods, to buy something, and then they would immediately leave. All the shelling that happened even before that, from the very beginning of the aggression, meant that the shells were landing in these central areas. We tried to draw the attention of the people not to gather in groups, but at that time you couldn't really do that. People were struggling to survive. They needed food. They needed too exchange goods. The police was in a difficult situation. We had to be on the street, too, to draw people's attention to the fact that they shouldn't be gathering in groups and to leave these places quickly, but it would always happen that the shelling would cause a lot of misfortune, a lot of deaths, a lot of wounding.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I wonder if it would be possible to return very briefly to the issue of the admissibility of what has now become P1987, and I wonder if I could just be heard outside of the presence of the witness on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, it's better. Mr. Djozo, there's one matter we'd like to discuss in the absence of yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, in looking at this document, first of all it required a permission to be added to the Rule 65 ter list because the history of this was that the notice was filed on the 22nd of October, which didn't include this document, and then on the 6th of December -- or the 8th of December a supplemental notice was filed in which this document was added, but that's a technical issue that normally wouldn't make any difference. But the unfairness of this is that on the 29th of October, which was after the first notice was filed but before this document was added, we heard the testimony of Mr. Miokovic, KDZ194, he's the author of the report that's been admitted, and so at that time we had no information that this incident would be part of the testimony and we didn't ask him any questions about it. Now, the difference between the testimony of this witness and Miokovic and the report is that this report indicates that the shells came from the Serb side and that UNPROFOR concurred with the direction of the shell that was concluded. This witness can't speak to that at all. So the result is that you've now admitted a report for which we've been prevented from cross-examining the witness who could have spoken to that, and we think that that's an unfairness and ought not to be allowed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your indulgence for a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: A couple of points I want to make, Your Honour. First of all, this document was disclosed in relation to Mr. Miokovic on 16 September 2010 under Rule 66(B), as authored by, and then on 8 December 2010 as a potential 65 ter exhibit. With respect to the document now with this witness, it's clearly a relevant document and relevant to this witness's evidence, Your Honour. So I think the more appropriate course may be, should Mr. Robinson want to raise this issue or deal with this document again with Mr. Miokovic, he could ask then to do so with Mr. Miokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a question from the top of my head, but is it not sufficient on the part of the Prosecution to have had Mr. Djozo's evidence that certain shells landed on this area on certain period of time instead of having this document admitted? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What is helpful about this document for the witness is that the witness during his initial testimony in the Perisic case was unable to date the incident other than approximately putting it in time about a month before Markale. The actual report of the incident which he -- which refreshed his memory on seeing it in preparation for his testimony provided a precise date for the incident. That would be -- and I think the date, Your Honour, is of assistance to all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So my question is do we need that report as such if that is the purpose of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I can have a moment to look at the actual report for a second, I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just before I answer your question, Your Honour, back as I said to the issue of fairness, the document was disclosed prior to Mr. Miokovic's testimony. They could have cross-examined Mr. Miokovic on it had they wanted to. That being said, I've had a look at the document. I've discussed it with Mr. Tieger, and given that the incident was explored with the witness in his written evidence and given his comments on the stand, I'm prepared to withdraw the document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. How about Exhibit P1990? Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's not the same situation, Mr. President, so it can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your understanding and co-operation, Ms. Edgerton. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apology for your inconvenience, Mr. Djozo. So you'll be asked by Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Karadzic, let's start your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djozo, good morning.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to tell me your father's name?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father's name is Alija Djozo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is Agan, Dzemal Agan, related to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you receive any kind of medal? Were you decorated in the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have any legal problems at any time earlier during the Communists or currently?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't have the information about your father. I have information about some other people with the same name as you, so please don't mind these questions. Can you please tell me how the introduction of the new authorities proceeded in your municipality after the first multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm apolitical. I wasn't really interested in politics, especially not in politics of nationalist parties, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the police in your municipality denied the implementation of an inter-party agreement and that the Serbs never got the police posts that they were supposed to have and that this caused a major crisis?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that, and I wasn't really paying any attention. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that before the war the chief of the public security station in the municipality of Stari Grad increased several times over the number of reserve policemen who were exclusively ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the aggression on Bosnia and Herzegovina, as far as I know, the majority of Serb police members left not only the Stari Grad police station but other police stations as well. And also, as far as I know, the police reserve force, according to the law in force at the time, could have been activated much earlier, and it was activated much earlier, before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm making this break because of the interpreters, so that you know why I'm waiting. This is precisely what I'm talking about, Mr. Djozo. The elections were in 1990. The Serbs were allocated certain posts at your police station. They never got those posts, and much before the war broke out, the chief of your station, I think his name was Bato or Dahic -- actually, who was the chief of the Stari Grad police station, please?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the police station in Stari Grad, the chief of the police station was Mr. Enes Bezdrob.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the commander. The commander of the station was Ismet Dahic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the commander of the station was Ismet Dahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time many scores of police officers were engaged in the reserve forces, including members of the underworld and criminals, and none of these extra reserve forces were Serbs. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in that police station, as well as in the other police station, there were no criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the reserve policemen that your station appointed and mobilised and to whom it issued weapons illegally and in contravention of the rules. Did you know that in your municipality the number of the reserve police forces was increased several times over, above and beyond the numbers allowed by law?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the police station and began to work there, that is all I know. I don't know what the classification of the post was before that. I never knew how many policemen you were supposed to have at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were a policeman when the war began. You began to work in June or July 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war broke out, I worked in Hidrogradnja. After that, when the war broke out, when it began, I reported to the Stari Grad Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of any investigations into the killing of Serbs in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such killings while I was in the Stari Grad police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Kazani located in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kazani is on the slopes of the Trebevic, and that is part of the Stari Grad area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that you never heard that Serbs were thrown into pits in Kazani, Serbs that had been captured on the streets of your municipality, taken out of their apartments, taken there and killed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this was something that was under the control of the army. I know that certain people were brought to trial who had committed certain crimes, but I wasn't directly involved in the commission of those acts or any other activities related to that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about your station? That is its area of responsibility. Did they conduct any investigations into the killings of Serbs in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no killings of Serbs in the area covered by the Stari Grad police station from the time that I was at the police station, from 1992 up to the present. There were no killings of Serbs. We didn't have information that Serbs were being killed in the manner that you have described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any other police station in the Stari Grad municipality?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only police station in Stari Grad is the Stari Grad police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the killings of citizens, is that something that falls under the jurisdiction of that police station?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the event of any kind of killing or murder, an investigation team is formed comprising the investigating judge, people from the CSB, from homicide and sexual crimes department, as well as the duty officer from the police station, from the sector where the crime was committed. These were crimes, so this was something that was under the jurisdiction of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The CSB at the level of?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who provided other operative services to the CSB inspectors? Is that -- that is -- is that something that is done by the local police station?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the event of any kind of a crime, the CSB is notified. It wasn't important whether it was a grave crime or not. An investigation team is formed after the police station is notified, and from each police station the duty officer and the duty crime technician had to attend the investigation, if it occurred, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that your authorities issued information and warnings that the chasing down and hunting of Serbs on the streets of your town is something that would no longer be tolerated?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know Musan Topalovic, Caco?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw that man. I did hear of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you present to the Trial Chamber what you know about Musan Topalovic, Caco.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really wondering what the relevance of this line of questioning is to this witness's proffered testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was wondering as well. Mr. Karadzic, we have only limited time. I would like you to move on to the topics which the witness covered in his direct examination, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I have to say a few words about this. I see that witnesses have been drawn, including General Karavelic. We see that we will not have an opportunity to test everything that the Prosecution put in the indictment. Now, we are dealing with an area that was a real torture house for the Serbs. It was his job, it was the competence of his police station and he seems to know everything about everything except what happened to the Serbs, which is a scandal. It was the jurisdiction of his police station. This is a question of credibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Move on to the real topics, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: P1988 is the document I would like to call up, the sketch that you made. And while we're waiting, Mr. Djozo, I'll tell you that Musan Topalovic, also known as Caco, and the man nicknamed Krusko and all the most notorious criminals were the gang leaders, the army leaders in your municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would recommend you to move on to the topics which will be covered by P1988.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1988. Then I will have no opportunity to test the credibility and the objectivity of this witness and his bias, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's unacceptable, Mr. Karadzic. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, please take a green pen this time, with the assistance of the usher. You marked the cathedral here, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I marked the cathedral.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between numbers 2 and 4, is there a place of worship missing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the Serbian Orthodox Church, I can draw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the faculty of economics is a building that belongs to that church? Can you mark that church which is actually a Serbian cathedral church?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would not agree, Mr. Djozo, that it overlooks that street. It is next door to the faculty of economics, between numbers 2 and 4, and this other complex of buildings is on Strossmayer Street.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this group of buildings at that belongs to the Serbian Orthodox Church, together with the residences in that same street, also belongs to people from the Serbian Orthodox Church, this entire group of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where is the church itself? Could you mark it with a circle.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a number there. Let's say 5.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you say that we were shooting at that church?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that we police officers had the duty with regard to all places of worship, and especially the Serbian Orthodox Church in the Stari Grad municipality, to protect and defend and give every assistance to those people, the people in this church as well as the old Serbian Orthodox Church in the Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once you mentioned the old church, I will mention the murder of that member of a wedding party on the 1st of March, and everything that happened in that connection. Do you remember that priest Paripovic who was driven around the town, made to wear some sort of board on his chest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, you suggested that this approaching fire had the purpose of approaching and targeting the Markale marketplace.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the people who moved around these streets, including Kulina Bana, for instance, these streets were not very busy, actually, and that goes for Ferhadija and the Sarajevo Defenders Street. They were not very busy. Most people circulated along the Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is, did this fire depicted in this picture as you drew it actually targeted Markale? Were the weapons trained and aimed at Markale?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite certain that the fire targeted the busiest street. I know that from my prior experience in the JNA during my regular military service. I was trained to be a mortar platoon commander, and during my training we practiced the proper way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that is the basis on which you conclude that the purpose was to target Marsal Tita street, which was a busy one.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning of the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please let's not waste time on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I just hear an awful lot of overlap between question and answer, Your Honour, and I think it might be difficult for our colleagues in the interpretation booths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djozo, because of that overlapping we couldn't hear your answer to the previous question, "From the very beginning of the aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina," and then on we couldn't hear anything. What did you say, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the very beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, the central part of Stari Grad municipality was constantly shelled, mainly civilian areas, areas swarming with civilians, and especially the neighbourhood of Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many shells fell on that street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't possibly know. Thousands of shells landed on Stari Grad, including Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street and the streets around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Out of all those thousands, can you single out 50 shells and tell us what the investigation found?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about the investigations I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, do you agree that the war in Sarajevo lasted for 42 months?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never counted those days and years. I know it was extremely hard. I had no time to think about that. I had a wife and two children, my father, my mother, brother, sister, sister-in-law, people who needed my help.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have respect for that, but let us concentrate on this: On what basis do you say that this was a case of ranging in, of test firing and adjusting the aim on this area? Where did these four shells come from?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several questions in one, but I will try. At that time the ballistics expert, who is the only one competent and responsible for such a statement, wrote that the shell had come from the area of Lukavica, Mount Trebevic, Vraca, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have that finding, that report, so that we can test that methodology?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the findings, all the expert reports are available to the Prosecution. I don't have any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the documentation we received concerning these incidents, there are no documents that could be put to the test. Which incident would you say was a case of ranging in, test firing and adjusting the aim?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not necessarily ranging in regarding any of these shells. We believe that the target was Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, which was an especially busy area with a marketplace. We know that there were large numbers of Sarajevo citizens there at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it's not something that you established on any basis. It's your assumption.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established later when so many people got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how many shells landed in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street in connection with Markale and the Markale Market?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the Markale I incident, one shell landed killing people who happened to be there. And in Markale II, where I didn't participate in the investigation, I only heard from the media reports that the shell landed outside the market, the shopping centre, and again killed people who were shopping there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that place, which is the only place or perhaps one of few places where people gathered in large numbers, over 360 days was targeted twice. Markale I a couple of months before this ranging in, and Markale II a couple of months after this ranging in. Now, after testifying that this was a case of ranging in and adjusting the aim, how do you explain that two shells only fell within one year at this most important target?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, many more shells landed in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, not just these two. These two were the most heinous crimes, causing many deaths. Otherwise, hundreds and thousands of shells landed on Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street and the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that it was something unprecedented, and it's even more unprecedented because it was all staged, but in your opinion, the impression you are trying to create is that we were lurking to target Sarajevans in their favourite gathering places, and in all that year we managed to hit Markale marketplace once and the Markale shopping centre once. In 1994 the Markale Market, and the Markale shopping centre in 1995. Now, where did other shells fall on these Markale shopping centre and markets?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is probably footage of the destroyed place of Stari Grad from all the shells that fell, where we can see how many buildings were damaged, how many people were hurt and killed. People did not only die in these two places. People were being killed all over Stari Grad municipality and all over the city of Sarajevo. Stari Grad was visible from every position of the Army of Republika Srpska. From every VRS position you could see where the shells were falling, what was going on down there. All that was broadcast on radio and television Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was all broadcast, albeit with a different explanation, by the then Serbian agency SRNA. They were saying that we are killing our own people, that I threw a grenade to hurt myself and my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am inviting you to stay away from generalisations. This is the busiest gathering place, despite all your warnings that it was dangerous. You are suggesting that we are ranging in and adjusting the aim to hit them when they gather in the largest number. We hit twice, you say, and we say that it's the work of your forces. From number 3, let's say, to the eternal flame, how many shells landed in this area which you say was the busiest in Sarajevo? Did any third shell fall there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you've just asked a dozen questions that I would take time to answer. Could you please hand them to me one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, not Sarajevo in general. You are saying that you couldn't prevent Sarajevan civilians from gathering in this place. The Serbs were aiming there. Tell me, when did another shell fall in that place?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot present my evidence and speak about how many shells landed there. I don't have those documents, but they do exist. They're in the Office of the Prosecution. All the shells that fell there were investigated by the Stari Grad police station, by the CSB in Sarajevo. All this was recorded and archived, made available to the Prosecution, and the Prosecution has this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you have no evidence that apart from these two shells, one of which hit the shopping centre and the other hit the market, you have no proof that a third shell ever fell on this busiest civilian gathering place.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, on this gathering place, Markale Market and Markale shopping centre. You suggested to the Trial Chamber that the Serbs were lying in wait to hit civilians in this busiest place. Was ever a third shell? Do you have proof or is this just an uncorroborated statement that won't stand up?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only was there a third, there were hundreds of shells that fell on this area. Just before this there was a document from which we see that shells hit Dzenetica Cikme street, Romanijska Street, and then again Mula Mustafe Baseskije, the area of Centar municipality. In Drvarksa Street children were killed. There was a secondary Catholic school there. The VRS was targeting places that were the busiest, where there were the most civilians. Most people moving around, most people living there and gathering there. We felt it in Sarajevo. We people who lived in Sarajevo felt it on our own skin. We know exactly how it worked, how people got killed. It's not only the Muslims who got killed, everybody did, Serbs, Muslims, Croats alike. Dozens and hundreds of children were killed. So many children, 1500 children were killed in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, none of this is true, but I'm asking you kindly to refrain from generalisations. Just tell us the things that you can prove. And you cannot give us any proof that a third shell ever fell on the only place where you couldn't prevent civilians from gathering, as you put it. Now, I'm asking you about these shells. Was it ever established, and using which methodology, that this came from the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shell number 3 killed two people, several were wounded. When we got there to the spot in Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, which is not more than 50 metres away from Markale, we found the mutilated body of a man, his brains spilled on the tarmac. The same happened in spot number 1 in my drawing. A number of people got killed there. This place was a spot where shells landed before, but what I remember most clearly was this time when two young men were killed, students of political science. They had the same first name and I believe the same birthday. People were killed at all hours, day and night. These -- this spot that is marked on my drawing is a place where hundreds of shells fell. In a number of cases we came and investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one thing. Was it established that these shells actually came from Lukavica or wherever you said they came from?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lukavica, Vraca, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that this fire was ranging in and preparing the weapons for the incident of the 28th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly the targeting of the civilians who were moving along Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street and the busiest places. As for that hit of Markale, there must be clues, there must be evidence. You should ask the people who fired these shells. Every commander of a mortar battery has a record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what is the time interval between these shells?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly, but it was within two hours, between 12.00 and 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that ever determined or not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been determined, because we were there. We know when the shells landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that when shell number 2 landed, or, let's say, shell number 3 landed, those people, those civilians, if they were civilians, just remained hanging around there to be hit again?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two hours is a long time. If the first shell landed around noon at number 1, and half an hour later another one fell in a different place, and yet half an hour later a shell landed in a third place, people have to move. At first they take cover in a basement. They wait. Nothing happens for 30 minutes. They come out, and they continue on their way, wherever they were going, and only then do the next shells fall. What we lived through in Sarajevo, and what we experienced during on-site investigations in extinguishing fires, in giving first aid, tells us that places were targeted a second time. It doesn't mean that when we come to investigate after a shell immediately landed that another one won't land soon again. Very often when the ambulance arrives, the shelling would restart. When fire brigades came to extinguish fires, those places were targeted again. And in Sarajevo, you have many firemen who got killed precisely on their job. And people who were trying to help the victims of an incident often got killed themselves in the process. It was a way of killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will need more time to explore this. One other witness has already said the same things, and I asked him how many investigators got killed by such a second shell, and he said no one. Give me one example of an incident where the on-site investigators were killed by a follow-up shell. Just one.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just with respect to that assertion of what another witness might have said, I'm actually not so sure that that's quite the case, and I wonder if we might have a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember having heard that a certain witness didn't remember such event. Albeit it's a very lengthy question, but could you answer the last question? Whether you can give one example of an incident where the on-site investigators were killed by a follow-up shell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only talk about the Stari Grad area, and I know that none of us were killed. But, yes, shelling continued while we were investigating sites, and we had to run for our lives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time. It's time to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We lost this additional marking. I was going to tender it together with the Serbian church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The usher's computer is having technical difficulty, and so we'll try again when we resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, do you remember that you marked on this sketch an Orthodox church, the area of it and the place where it is? Could you do that again with the green pen. Just wait till the Usher is assisting you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to sketch approximately how it was. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put number 5 on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djozo. That will be admitted as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at P1528 in the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to deal with Sedrenik, Mr. Djozo, and then later we will come back to the centre of the town to throw light on certain matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the upper right-hand corner, please. And again the upper right-hand corner, please. A little bit more if possible, this upper right-hand corner, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, does this help you now to orient yourself and to mark the top of Grdonj, Sedam Suma, Pasino Brdo, Streliste, and to show us where Barice and Mrkovici are too?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barice and Mrkovici you cannot see here. They're probably on some other part of the map. We do have Sedam Suma. Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put the number 1 near Sedum Suma, and can you mark the trig point of Grdonj. Can you circle that. And can you mark Spicasta Stijena now, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to do that here. Let's say it's somewhere here above the actual settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you mark Pasino Brdo now, Streliste, Hladivode.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Streliste more or less, because a large part of this area is described as Streliste but actually doesn't occupy all of that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us -- now, actually, can you indicate where the line of separation was according to your best recollection? If you can do it with blue.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take part in these actions in this -- any combat action, so I really am not able to say where the lines are. What I know for sure is that it was somewhere here or around Spicasta Stijena, a little bit above, but I cannot be absolutely sure. I wasn't there ever. It's somewhere up towards the Smreke and Barice. I had heard that it was -- that there where the lines were. I've never actually been to the lines, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Djozo, red marking seen behind the blue line, just to the right side of the trig point, refers to the -- I forgot that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that refers to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it's sufficient, yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, the peak of Grdonj, the actual trig point, was under the control of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian army; is that correct? And this blue line would need to be a little bit more to the north in relation to the trig point.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know for sure is that Spicasta Stijena was taken up by the Army of Republika Srpska. They took it right at the beginning of the war. That is where they dug in, and they stayed there till the end, right up until just before integration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the southern slope of Grdonj? Who had control of that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grdonj's a large area. I can mark it. You can see in the middle of the map towards the top that it also says Grdonj. Grdonj is a large area of Sarajevo where people were living then and are still today. I was in the Stari Grad municipality area working at the Stari Grad police station throughout the whole war, so I'm not really knowledgeable about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I was hoping that you would know where the lines were. Most people that we had here before knew where the lines were, so I thought you would too. We don't need to tender this, but do you agree that Sedam Suma are below Grdonj and around the peak of Grdonj? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sedam Suma is also a large area that was forested and a part of the forest was cut down during the war. It's a wooded area. When I said that it was known where the lines were approximately, that would also include the cutting of the trees that were in that area. So the area where the trees were cut would indicate that there were no lines as soon as you actually entered the woods, that would mean that these were the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would a photograph help you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at 1D2869.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you happy to lose this, Ms. Edgerton, his markings? Maybe on the system.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm happy to lose those, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2869.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the panorama of that area. If necessary, we can zoom in. Can you mark the peak of Grdonj here, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I can. It would be good to zoom in a little bit on this part.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the horizon, please. We can cut off a little bit more of the sky if necessary. Let's do a little bit more zooming in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you now please mark the peak of Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The peak of Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An arrow from the sky pointing down to the peak. And if you can put the number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is where we see some relay installations. They were there before the war also.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not familiar with the terrain before the war, because I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now mark Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to draw a line where Spicasta Stijena is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you put the number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark Pasino Brdo now?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasino Brdo or Streliste is located to the right, behind this part where you can see that the trees are cut, Pasino Brdo is behind this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We're going to see that later. Can you now mark the area where the trees were cut during the war.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to indicate that with a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that with the number 3.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this clearing was made during the war. People cut the trees down in order to have wood for heating; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Sedrenik, the Sedrenik settlement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Sedrenik. There aren't too many houses there, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many houses are there. We never thought about how many there were, but there is a significant number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the top where the arrow indicates Grdonj was in the hands of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be certain of that. I was never there. I really couldn't say whether it was in the hands of the Army of Republika Srpska or the B and H Army. At least the area where the line of separation was. The only thing that I'm sure of is that we were never safe passing in this area. Through the settlement and along the settlement there is a street here, Sedrenik, that you can pass. We were never safe there. When you say Spicasta Stijena, this is the place marked with the number 2. There were several trenches along the surface of Spicasta Stijena. They were quite long. The line and the trenches were not only in this part where the Army of Republika Srpska was, but it stretched along this edge, along the top of Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In a different case it was established that the lines were on the northern slope of Grdonj and in that area, right up until Spicasta Stijena, they were only 20 metres apart. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Djozo, just a second. No, it's totally unacceptable to refer to a decision in other cases. Reformulate your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not talking about a decision but actually I referred to testimony from another case, but very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that both sides had lines here, the B and H Army and the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that they were there, but I don't know where the lines were and which areas they covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Mrkovici and Barice or the population in that area that comprised that army, did they ever try to capture the settlement or the neighbourhood of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who made up the Army of Republika Srpska. In the same way that I heard that there were some attacks. Allegedly there is a tower behind which was the subject of a dispute of some firing, but I really don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina carried out numerous offensives via Spicasta Stijena in an attempt to break through to Barice and Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is even -- that is something that I know even less about. I don't know anything about attempts to reach the peak of Spicasta Stijena, because from the very beginning, the Army of Republika Srpska was there. It was very hard to capture this, and we saw that during the reintegration. We could see bunkers. We could see roads laid down, trenches, that this was very professionally done, and it wasn't possible to capture that area. As far as I know, there were no attempts for the army to enter Barice through Spicasta Stijena. Mrkovici is much farther than Barice. I'm really not able to give you a definite answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that as a soldier or a policeman trenches and bunkers are not an offensive tool but a defensive tool?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's not for the witness. Could you come to the issues which the witness can give answers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, you said yesterday that this forest was cut down, the trees and the woods were cut down for firewood during the war. This is one assertion. The other assertion is that the Serbs did not fire at the people who were cutting down the trees. Some understanding of yours, a third matters is why the Serbs didn't shoot is that -- is because it suited the Serbs to have these trees cut down. Can you please tell us from a military point of view why would it suit the Serbs that these trees be cut down?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska allowed this to happen because it meant that this terrain was cleared. It wouldn't be possible to approach the area. They could see who was moving there, if anyone was moving around in that area. So this was something that created a kind of secure area for them. They knew what was going on and how far people were moving, how far the lines were, but I really don't know if there were any lines there. In the first place, I didn't come to this place, and I didn't cut down any firewood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you came to this place to cut down the trees, did you cross the Muslim lines or were they further ahead?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness did go there to cut down trees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't notice at any point any lines. I was there approximately where these houses are. There was -- there was some trees there that were not cut down, and people would come there. This other part to the right indicated with a dotted line is an area that I never went to and I don't know if there were any lines were -- I don't know if there were any lines, and if there were, I don't know where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are speculating about the reasons why the Serbs didn't fire. Do you have any proof of that or is that just something that you concluded?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would go there at night. I myself also went there at 2.00 or 3.00 in the morning to cut down a tree. The others did the same thing. We didn't go there during the day. Had we gone there during the day, things probably wouldn't have been the same. They could have heard something, cutting going on. They could have assumed that trees were being cut, but they didn't shoot. During the day we didn't dare go to that area. Whoever moved around in that area from Sedrenik, they would get shot at, and many people were killed and wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll hear about that later on, but you probably knew that the army had night-vision capabilities and they could have seen what was going on at night. They could have just disregarded this action, and they could have decided not to do anything. In other words, are you saying that they heard that something was being done but that they didn't know exactly what was being done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, how could this witness know what other people heard or didn't hear. That's a question nobody can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now please date and initial this photograph, and then we can tender it.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put the date and your initials. That's 10th of December, I take it. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly look at 1D01958. Do you agree that this is the security administration of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the BiH, dated the 29th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm seeing this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. You're seeing it for the first time, but is that what it says? Is this the bulletin of the security administration of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying I'm seeing this for the first time. This is the first time that I'm looking at this document. I've never seen a document which says that it is the bulletin of the security administration of the Supreme Staff command. So I can see what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 4 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, could you please read the two paragraphs from the top. Could you please read that out loud.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that on the 26th of July, 1993, wood was being cut down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read this?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 26th of July, 1993, a group of civilians at Vilsonovo Setaliste, in front of the positions of the HVO units was cutting down trees. It's indicative that the aggressor did not fire even though they had clearly visible targets in front of them. Soldiers of the HVO drove the civilians away upon the intervention of fighters of the 10th Mountain Brigade and the aggressor opened fire only after the civilians left. "On the 25th of --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. You don't need to read further. Mr. Djozo, do you see that in the middle of town at Vilsonovo Setaliste in front of the positions of the HVO units civilians were cutting down trees and the Serbian Army did not fire until the civilians went away?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says here. I mean, nothing is being disputed in this particularly because Vilsonovo Setaliste, Wilson's Promenade, is along the Miljacka River, along the line of separation. The Army of Republika Srpska was located at Grbavica, and depending on how you look at it, I don't know exactly where the positions were, they were in some of those buildings. It's possible that they didn't shoot. It's possible that there was nobody there at that particular time, so they didn't see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The river is 50 metres broad there, so that is the distance between the lines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the breadth of the river. Then there is the bank of the Miljacka River, and then on the other side you have the promenade. You've got the street, and then you have buildings as well. That's on one side. And then you have the same thing on the other side. Vilsonovo Setaliste is a long street stretching along through Sarajevo all the way to the centre.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this document now. This is a document produced by the BH Army, and that's not in dispute. It's indisputable. Can this be admitted, because this also sheds some light on the cutting of the wood on Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I have no idea how this sheds any light on the cutting of the wood in Grdonj. However, the witness has read a paragraph into the record and commented on it. I don't see why we need the document which is four pages long any further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the record is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber tends to agree with Ms. Edgerton, but we'll admit only this part of this document. So this part, this paragraph on page 4, will be admitted when the translation is over. So in the meantime, we will put that marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D910, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see 65 ter 7048 on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's P1058 as well, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
