utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to appear, Mr. Djozo, could you tell us which brigades were active and operated in the area covered by your police station, in your precinct, in other words? Which BH Army brigades operated there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know there was a brigade, or maybe not even a brigade-strength unit in the area of Grdonj, Sedrenik, at Bistrik in the Trebevic area, but which brigade specifically, I really don't know that I can comment on that. We did not have much in common with the army. We did not co-ordinate our actions with them, nor did we have access to their areas of responsibilities. They had their own area of responsibility and we had ours, the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, look at this map. Would you agree would me that it says a working map of the Chief of Staff, the command of the 12th Division of the land forces, and then it says the beginning is on the 1st of January, 1995, and end at 1019 hours.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please zoom in on the position where it says the municipality Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please pause. Now you can continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Sedrenik the area of responsibility of the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that. I was not a member of the army. I wasn't a member of that brigade, and I don't know what their area of responsibility was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you said that Sedrenik was a civilian settlement or neighbourhood. Now, my question is: Was Sedrenik a military area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sedrenik neighbourhood was a civilian area, a civilian settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now zoom in on Stari Grad municipality. We saw the title and the source of this document, and now I would like us to focus and zoom in on the town itself. Let's focus on the eastern part. This is the west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where the number 115 appears, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now we have the area of Stari Grad. Could we now zoom in on the right-hand portion. Perhaps one more time, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, would you please mark Grdonj hill, and we can also see the trig point on the map for Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we -- could you please put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please put a circle around Grdonj settlement and Sedrenik settlement.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we could zoom in a little more it would be easier, but I'll try to do it. It's approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the Grdonj neighbourhood or settlement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I see trig points here, I cannot see any houses there, and I'm not sure whether this is actually the settlement, because on the other map I saw on the right-hand side where it said Grdonj. Now, here we can see it, and I can underline that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the word "Grdonj" is printed, but the staff of the 2nd Battalion was in Grdonj settlement, correct? That's the little arrow where it says number 2.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The arrow with the number 2 is there, but where the staff was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what the arrow is indicating. Now, below that can you see that there is a symbol for a mortar?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what a mortar symbol is. Do you mean this round circle, black circle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the dome with these two antennae, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo is saying that he is not aware of this kind of map. There is no point in continuing that line of questioning. Put your case to the witness and see how we can go from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please now underline Barice village and Donje Biosko village. You mentioned those in your evidence.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can locate Barice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, to the right of that is Donje Biosko.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I also see Odzak, it's here somewhere. Donje Biosko should be around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please now underline Hladivode?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, would you please put a circle around the staff of the 1st Battalion, because this little flag there, symbol, indicates that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the "3BB"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, where "1BB" is. Mr. Djozo, am I correct that you marked as Sedrenik only a tiny hamlet, whereas the Sedrenik settlement is actually the area where the headquarters of the 1st Battalion is?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Sedrenik is an area. It is an entire area. It can be larger or smaller, but the settlement itself, just at the foot of Spicasta Stijena, that's what I marked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the place below, that's not Sedrenik settlement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's very hard to see how far it stretches actually on a map of this type. It's not very large.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please underline Donje Mrkonje. Can you see that? That's above Barice.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, the 3rd Mountain Battalion, where was it deployed? The staff, its headquarters. 3BB? Is that in Barutana?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Barutana is, as far as I know, the settlement along Moscanica river -- or rather, stream. You can't really see Sedrenik from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where the headquarters of the 152nd Brigade -- or, rather, these are not -- this is not the brigade level. These are the 2nd and 3rd Battalions, indicated with the arrow.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 152nd Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, right in front of it you see numbers 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's around here that the barracks at Vratnik were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please just put a circle at the bottom of those two little flags?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we might have a problem because we didn't put any numbers next to these, but we can go back to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I waited with patience. I told you to put your case to the witness. Now I think it's the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My case is the following, Mr. Djozo: This entire area was militarised and very densely populated by military troops, that the brigade had 5.500 to 6.000 soldiers, and they had their headquarters and all the infrastructure of the 1st and 2nd Battalion of the 152nd Brigade, and also the battalions of the 105th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how many troops there were there. If the number is 5.000, that's really a large number, but I have no clue how many men there were in those units, where those units were, where their headquarters were. I know nothing of any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look where there is a number 105 written in on a small -- on this little flag that is not a triangular shape but rather like a rectangle, and then there a slope, an angle there. Where it says 105, that's in the very centre of town where the shells fell. You see there it says 105 and 152. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I wonder if this is Bjelave or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's Trampina Street. Would you agree with me that Trampina Street runs along the eastern border of the main park?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Trampina Ulica. I assume -- I mean I never actually walked along that street. I know of it. If someone were to ask me now, Could you take me to Trampina street, I probably couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Would you please mark Hamdije Kresevljakovica Street here and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second before we go on. Mr. Djozo, you said you did not know how many troops there were there. Does this mean that you do not dispute the location of those several military units that existed at the time as indicated by this map, irrespective of their strength?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first of all, I don't know when this map was marked, what year this relates to, and what it really depicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The card is the 15th -- of the 15th of March, 1995. That's when this operation was to commence, and it was to end in September, sometime in September. Now, as you know, this situation did not -- the military situation here did not change from 1992 all the way up until the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, I'm a police officer. I was only a policeman. I did not have any contact with the military. They were not our superiors. They did not command us or order -- issue any orders to us. I can see what's written on this map, but what this actually depicts, I don't know. I've never actually been to any of those locations marked there, where you say that there are headquarters or commands, so this doesn't really say much to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But, Mr. Djozo, you testified here that Serbs actually targeted civilians and civilian targets, that Sedrenik was a civilian neighbourhood, that there was no military justification for opening fire. Now, my question is: Do you know or do you actually dispute that in your precinct there were 105th, 152nd, and 115th Brigades deployed with a number of attached companies? So do you deny that these troops were actually deployed in this confined area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say either way. I know that there were some troops there. Now, what brigades or how many of them or what the manpower was, I don't know anything about that, who their commanders were or anything of that sort. I've heard of some of this, but I don't know whether they were deployed here or in some other area. Sedrenik is a civilian neighbourhood, was a civilian neighbourhood, where the people who were from that part of Sarajevo lived. Of course, some of them had already left because they could not bear the pressure, and they tried to escape the shelling and the sniper fire that was opened on them from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Now, would you agree with me that Mehina Kafana is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the place. Could the accused please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is Mehina Kafana on the main road there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of Mehina Kafana, or Meho's cafe, but I had never been there. I don't know where that cafe is. If it is here on that road above the cemetery. I don't know where that road leads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just help us, please. Where we see number 12 next to Skenderija, which means the headquarters of the 12th Division --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, in relation to this map, I think we heard everything we can hear from the witness from his previous answer. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you understand, Mr. Djozo, now that your statement that this is a civilian neighbourhood and that fire was opened on civilian areas is not really true? And can you see that there were a lot of military installations there? Do you see all the infrastructure that was entered on this map? Do you agree that this is actually a militarised area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the Army of Republika Srpska, the hospital was also considered a military area, as well as the maternity hospital. Now, you should know best, because you were the supreme commander and you knew what kind of orders were issued and how everything was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please put your signature and date on this and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be helpful to understand witness's evidence. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D911, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You took part in a number of investigations into sniping incidents in Sedrenik, and you testified in two cases before this Tribunal, in the Milosevic and Perisic cases; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I participated in a number of on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Milosevic case, you said that there were some 100 sniper victims in Sedrenik, many of them children who were on their way to school, whereas in the Perisic case you corrected yourself, and you said that there were some 50 to 100 victims of the shelling and sniping incidents together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took part in some on-site investigations where children, women, and elderly were killed, and about two months ago, I was with some acquaintances, sitting. We were chatting and talking about -- reminiscing and discussing the wartime events and days, and there was a person in my company who mentioned that she was in Sedrenik throughout the war and that her father had been killed in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please stay away from people's stories. Now, in your amalgamated statement, in paragraph 20 and also in your statement of 25 November 1995, you said that there were hundreds of victims killed in the sniping, and later on, you said that the number of victims in total was somewhere between 50 and 100 victims who were killed both in shelling and sniping incidents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to allow me to finish what I was trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, but my time is limited, and the stories that were told to you in a cafe, well, we don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add something to your previous answer, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Talking with this person, she told me, actually, that her father had been killed at Sedrenik, that his name was Ibrahim Podrug, and that he was hit by a sniper, and that his abdominal artery was severed. I told that person that I actually took part in that on-site investigation, but I did not actually see the victim because he had already been taken to hospital at Kosevo. And then she told me, "Well, you know, it was then broadcast on Radio Sarajevo that he was the 100th victim, the 100th man who was killed by fire opened from Spicasta Stijena. So that's what I was trying to say. In other words, we did know, we did have some information about the approximate figure, that over a hundred people were killed up there in sniping or shelling incidents. But what was so striking was that I heard this story about this man, Ibrahim Podrug, who was actually named as the 100th victim of fire opened from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I will put it to you, Mr. Djozo, that there were not 100, far from 100 victims. There weren't even ten in total. But can we please now rely on your knowledge, because you are a police officer who is testifying here about your investigations that you participated in.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to comment, Mr. Djozo, on Mr. Karadzic's statement that it's not -- there were not far from 100 victims, there weren't even 10 in total.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: And of those ten, some were just grazed and wounded by the fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that is a ridiculous statement. We know exactly how many people were killed. We kept a record, and I'm just telling you here this bit of information that Ibrahim Podrug was the 100th victim of fire opened from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I really appreciate what you've just said on condition that we actually be provided the material that you are quoting there, that you actually know the exact number of victims, of civilians, who had been killed by Serb fire. Now, can you tell us Sehid's were there in Sedrenik and how many victims were victims of Sehid fire? Do you know that or not? How many war casualties were there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't. How could I know, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 65 ter 09713.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is a report of an on-site investigation where you were the duty officer at the public security station in Stari Grad; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see which record it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The wounding of Dervisa Selmanovic.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I investigated this site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you did the on-site investigation report based on the statement of a physician at the hospital and the statement of Dervisa Selmanovic herself whom you later visited at her home?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can describe how it was. Somebody informed the police station Stari Grad that a bullet was fired by a firearm from Spicasta Stijena, hitting Dervisa Selmanovic. I informed the investigating judge on duty, and according to the Law on Criminal Procedure, Article 154, had the right and authorised me and a scenes of crime officer and ballistics experts from CSB Sarajevo to go on the site and investigate, and we did. We did not find Dervisa there, because the incident happened around 10.00, 11.00. She had gone out into her own yard at number 56 in order to collect firewood when she was hit in the left upper leg. That's the information we got. She had been taken to the hospital where it was found that her injury was light. We only photographed the site but were unable to interview Ms. Selmanovic on the spot. We just got that information from the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2436, please. I believe this is an associated Prosecution exhibit. Isn't it? If not, I tender this record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Report of this witness, 9713?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought the Prosecution had tendered this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I get a confirmation from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, we did not, because it relates to a dropped incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to tender that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D912, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, could you now mark the place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I don't believe in my memory -- we had English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark the house of Dervisa Selmanovic, the place where you went on the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows Spicasta Stijena, the Sedrenik settlement, and the Vahid cemetery. I can mark the settlement, but I can't mark the house. I did not even photograph this. It was the scenes of crime officer who took photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then mark the settlement which includes her house and put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you put number 2 at the top of Grdonj hill.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's where the aerials are. I'm not sure. I can only be sure about Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark Spicasta Stijena then.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which method did you use to determine that the shot came from Spicasta Stijena rather than any other location on this picture?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ballistics man determined exactly where it came from, but according to the neighbours of Dervisa Selmanovic, the witnesses, we know how she was standing, where she was standing, and where she was facing, and where the bullet could have come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see the report of that ballistics expert to check that. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reports are with the court and the prosecutor's office in Sarajevo. None of us acted on our own behalf. We could only investigate on-site by authorisation from the Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you want to say that there was a trench of the VRS there, or perhaps it was behind Spicasta Stijena, in the field?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, when we toured these trenches, it was not just one trench. Trenches ran across this length, and there were several sniper emplacements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with blue the lines of Bosnia and Herzegovina Army and the red -- and in red the VRS lines.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to be able to, but I don't know where those military defence lines were. What I know is that in this area of Sedrenik settlement there were none. I went there with the police patrol leader, and there were no trenches of the ABH army there. We didn't go any further in this sector. This is already the sector covered by the Centar police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the top of Grdonj do you dispute that there were ABH lines and trenches?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they were there or in some other place, I don't know. I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you dispute that to the east of Spicasta Stijena there were BH Army lines facing Serbian lines which were in the woods and behind the woods? Not on Spicasta Stijena itself but to the east. Is it true that there were ABH lines?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again I've never been to visit those lines. I don't know where they were. It's possible that they were there, but I've never really seen them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. I wanted to remind you that you'll have about -- a bit more than an hour left. The witness is not aware of the confrontation line or such things. I would recommend you to concentrate on more important issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Is it true that this area around the mosque also belongs to the Sedrenik settlement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that this mosque is recent. It was maybe opened a year ago, and new houses were built there. There are many new houses. A new school was built. It's been 18 years since the war. All this is growing and getting larger and larger, and this area is sort of blending with Sedrenik. I know that there is a settlement or a neighbourhood called Bakije. Every street, every neighbourhood has its own name. This area at the foot of Spicasta Stijena is Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your initials and date, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D913, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that next to Mehina Kafana, in a privately owned house, the HQ of the 105th Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you understood HQ to mean. I never went there. If there were any commands there, I don't know where they were. I don't know in which building it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The BH Army documents referred to the house next to Mehina cafe. In your report, however, to move to another subject, you said that Dervisa Selimovic was injured in her left leg, but according to other documents she was wounded in the right leg.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first reports that we, in the police, received was that she was wounded in the leg. We were not able to interview her, so we had to find her and talk to her. Since she lived in Sedrenik previously, she left Sedrenik maybe she was because she was wounded there, but subsequently, I don't know how much later, a month or more later, we managed to locate her. It was not far from Kosevo Hospital. Dzemal Alica [phoen] Street, I believe. And we wanted to talk to her to see how she was wounded, what actually had happened. I went to that address. I found Mrs. Selmanovic, sat down together with her, took her medical file that she kept with her. I photocopied it, and it was established from talking to her and from the documents that she was wounded not in the leg that the witnesses and other people in the hospital told us but in the other leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that she herself once said before investigators that she was wounded in the left leg and another time that she was wounded in the right leg? If you want me to, I'll call up a document.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of statements she made. After talking to her in her apartment where she was residing, I never saw her again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly take a look at 1D2810.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a lot of time we've spent now on an incident that's been dropped and dropped for quite some time, and I'm just wondering the utility of this as this was not part of the witness's proffered evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said it was dropped. Was it in the indictment at all, or is it just one of the unscheduled incidents?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll tell you exactly when it was dropped in a few moments, but, no, it's not an unscheduled incident either.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was someone convicted for this incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll verify, but I think it was dropped in the first 73 bis filing, 31 August 2009, but I will verify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. In any event, I'm just -- I was wondering -- I was posing the same question to myself. Where are you leading with this line of questions which is not included in the indictment and never touching upon the items the witness dealt with in his chief evidence? Probably we may exercise more robust exercise in limiting your time, Mr. Karadzic. Let's continue. What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Excellency, this about Spicasta Stijena, where there were no trenches, no snipers, whereas this witness testified in another case and General Milosevic was convicted for this incident. I want to show that this entire investigation was arbitrary and geared at blackening and convicting Serbs, and this is a pattern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with your trial, Mr. Karadzic. What are you going to ask in relation to the judgement we are seeing at this moment? What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, in which case and using which methodology did you precisely determine that somebody shot somebody from Spicasta Stijena? Please direct us to that evidence.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the records, all the evidence, all the on-site investigations conducted into firing incidents from Spicasta Stijena are kept at the Cantonal Court and the High Court in Sarajevo, and every time there was an investigating judge and somebody from the CSB Stari Grad present. Ballistics experts made determinations, and according to the information I have, including some information shown me here again, the UNPROFOR agreed also with the conclusions made concerning sniping from Spicasta Stijena. In every on-site investigation, the ballistics expert is the only one qualified to make determinations regarding sniping from Spicasta Stijena. What we were able to see, police officers from the criminal investigations department and scenes of crime officers, was evidence on site and clues, and we could just see with our own eyes that the shot could only have come from Spicasta Stijena to hit people and children in Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there were armed men only along that 50-metre stretch. What about the rest of that whole area up to 180 degrees? Were there any other armed men?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place where Dervisa Selmanovic was standing was sheltered from all other sides except for Spicasta Stijena. Her family, when they were building that house, could never have imagined when they were building the house that one day there would be a sniper on Spicasta Stijena who would target the family. Her house was located in such a way that she had to go outside into the yard to collect firewood to make a fire, and it just so happened that she was hit at that moment, and it's up to those humans -- or, rather, non-humans who were on Spicasta Stijena firing at people, women and children. I believe that is borderline abnormal behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's stick to the facts. You know where the house was. You know that it was sheltered from three sides of the world and it was -- it was vulnerable only on the side of Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: An on-site investigation team went to the place, photographed the location. They also photographed Spicasta Stijena, of which they had a clear view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you state that Dervisa Selmanovic was a homemaker, and she was, in fact, a cook in the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I talked to her, when I asked her about her occupation, she said she was a housewife. I could not imagine that she would not be speaking the truth. I took her at her word. She was in her home when she was wounded. She was making a fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of the people, civilians, who were killed in Sedrenik. As a police officer, member of on-site investigation teams, give us those names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Djozo. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just before we go much further into this, I told Your Honour I'd verify and, indeed, this is an incident that was never charged in the indictment. So this is an unscheduled incident on which the Prosecution has not led any evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was the point of my question. It was never in the indictment --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It was never in the indictment but I wasn't able to give you an accurate answer without checking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But let me remind everyone, with all due respect, that in the examination-in-chief and in his statement, this witness mentioned that Sedrenik was a civilian settlement and that between 50 and 100 people were killed by sniping from Spicasta Stijena. I'm now asking not only about Dervisa Selmanovic. I'm asking the witness which methods he used to rule out all other possibilities and determine that the firing came from Spicasta Stijena and to give us the names of those 50 or I don't know how many civilians who actually got killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm wondering where the witness gave evidence to the effect that he decided the direction of the fire or the origin of the fire himself. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you, Mr. Djozo, determine that the fire only came from Spicasta Stijena, not from any other place? Not only in the case of Dervisa Selmanovic but in all the other cases.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the only one who is qualified to make an official determination as to the direction of fire is the ballistics expert. He is an expert in these matters. All the rest of us from the criminal investigations department and from the scenes of crime department who were there could see that a shot hitting that place could only have come from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the distance between Spicasta Stijena and the place where Dervisa Selmanovic resided is more than 1.100 metres?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. And at that time, we did not have -- at least I did not have any instruments to measure the distance. I'm not sure it's more than 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's us then conclude. You are unable to give us the names of those civilians who were killed in the Sedrenik settlement, or are you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is very ugly to use the names of victims in this way. The lists exist. They are available. You can see exactly how many people in total, how many women, how many elderly, how many children were killed. But if you say there were 2.000 people killed in the sinking of the Titanic and you wanted me to give their names, this would be comparable to what you're actually asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the name of Tarik Zunic, from an incident in February, familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this last name Zunic somewhere from Sedrenik, but you would have to give me more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you all the names of people who were wounded. Tarik Zunic was wounded in 1995. Vahid Balta, 1995. Sanela Dedovic, wounded. I don't know exactly where, but she testified here on 29 January 2007 in the Milosevic case, and Tarik Zunic on the 7th of February, 2007. Mr. Djozo, for 1.260 days, the Serbs were defending Barice and Mrkovici, and they never attacked Grdonj or Sedrenik, and you couldn't find ten civilians killed in all that time that -- whose names you could give us.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo there were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, Sedrenik, Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Give us proof.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not the one collecting proof here. Why don't you find proof that it is just ten people, not over ten or over 100?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, for instance, that towards the end of May 1995 and early June, mid-June, and all the way up to mid-July, a major Muslim offensive was underway, and it affected Sedrenik, including planned, documented attacks aimed at Barice and Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the crime investigations department of the police at the time, and if there had been such planned actions, I wouldn't know about them. I was not a high-ranking officer who would have been involved in the making of such plans, so I can't tell you anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But as a citizen of Sarajevo, you were aware that there was shooting all over the place. You investigated some it have as a policeman. Are you trying to tell us now that there was no offensive at the time, that instead these shells were fired by the Serbs out of blue, for no reason at all? Just tell us, was there an offensive or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, this is not a cross-examination. This is an argumentative dialogue. You're putting submissions to the witness, disguising them as questions. It really isn't helping the Tribunal to determine the effective issues in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a break now, after which you will have three-quarters of an hour, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would just like to say that I'm ready to cross-examine the next witness for a shorter period of time if we can have a little extra time with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, you testified that there were some improvised bombs which were made from gas cylinders filled with explosives and placed on car tyres and released down the sides of the Trebevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at an investigation, not because of that, but because a man was killed in a street in Sirokaca Street, because he had initiated a trip mine, and we went to investigate. This is below Osmice. And people who were living there took us around and showed us how there were a number of improvised devices in one place. I did hear about this earlier, that such things did happen, that these devices were made, that oil drums were filled and that wheels were attached to them. I wanted to see what this was about. I went up there, and I could see gas cylinders made in exactly the same way. The only thing is that you couldn't really get close to that part, because the terrain was unsafe, and people said that there were minefields laid down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that you saw an unexploded gas cylinder in a minefield below the Lukavica-Pale road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't me at an investigation but one of my colleagues was there when, from Trebevic towards Katusevic [phoen], a part of the Old Town, such a barrel was released. The Serbian Army did that. And the barrel exploded near a house, causing a lot of material damage. As far as I can remember, nobody was killed, but I know that people said that the house which was struck by the barrel was completely destroyed, and that's where I saw the barrels and these gas cylinders to which wheels were attached. Wheels were welded on each side of these gas cylinders and these oil drums, and you could tell by the tyres that these were tyres from a military Deutz vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a photograph of this device or object that you just described for us?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote an official note about it, and I sent it to my police station. I explained what this was about. But as I said, you couldn't go up there because of the minefields. I did see a photograph of that here at the OTP. They showed it to me. They wanted to show me the photograph. They said, "Is this what that was?" And then I answered affirmatively.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to ask to find this photograph so that you can show us what sort of an improvised device this is that requires so much work. It needs an axle and then wheels need to be welded onto this part on each side. It's a lot of work.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One wheel is on one side, and another wheel is on the other side. This is not something that is very precise when it's released, but it does have a considerable destructive power when it explodes in a settlement, for example. Of course, there are photographs. One can see the object and how much work it needs. I don't know how people -- to what extent people were trained to make something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You saw an unexploded gas cylinder with wheels and another unexploded oil barrel that had wheels attached to it. Did this perhaps not call for a detailed investigation and photo documentation, and was such an investigation every carried out?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never did such an investigation, because I'm not qualified for that. Probably somebody else did that. I don't know if they were in the CSB or in the military unit, but I did see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D02408 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for this in the e-court, Mr. Djozo, can you please tell us what kind of a terrain is required for this barrel to be able to move in the desired direction?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need a steep terrain, and you know that the Army of Republika Srpska in that area was above the road. It was holding the Osmice road, and these barrels were released from there, from that height.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the Osmice hostel on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can. This is a photograph from an area long past. You can see the vegetation has grown back, the houses have been repaired, and all of this greenery has covered over the clearing that was there during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the upper right-hand quadrant, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that these trees that are 3 or 4 metres tall were not there during the war and that they grew back after the war, and since they were not there at the time, this device could roll down the slope but now it would not be possible for it to roll down the slope?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the trees were not so high, and you can see the bushes that are a metre or so high. This photograph does not faithfully represent what was there. You can see part of the gorge near Osmice, and that's what I saw when I was there carrying out the investigation at the time. There were houses in that area, and I think that you can see them in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you to circle the Osmice bed and breakfast and mark it with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you activate the marker, please, and can we again zoom in on this upper right-hand quadrant, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. That is fine. It's not quite clear on the photograph. Well, this the bed and breakfast Osmice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For your information, Mr. Karadzic, having heard your cross-examination so far, for which you have spent more than two hours, the Chamber is not minded to give you any further extension -- any extension to the time for your cross-examination of this witness. So try to conclude in the given time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be in half an hour; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A bit more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, are you able to indicate where the separation line is here, indicating what is under the control of the B and H Army and what is under the control of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that the road that I can indicate here with a dotted line -- [In English] That I put -- [Interpretation] We will mark the road with a number 2. That is the road that leads from Vraca to Trebevic. And that road could only be used by the Army of Republika Srpska and probably by civilians from Lukavica. This was the Lukavica-Pale road. I know that we never managed -- I could never manage to get there. We could move only in the settlements below Osmice. The Sirokaca, Cicin Han, Vasin Han, and Bogusevac settlements. Thus, this is where we came out for investigations, because this is where shells were landing. People were getting killed. There were investigations being conducted in these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please now mark where you saw this device which the Serbian Army allegedly produced and filled with explosives?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in the part where the road is cut, close to the number 2. There is a large slope here which I will indicate like this, and you can see the settlement down below. You can see the houses. I will put a number 3 there. I cannot remember exactly which house it was where I was, but I went there, and I could see where these four arrows are that I will mark with the number 4, that is the place where I could see these gas cylinders with wheels attached and a number of barrels that probably had oil or petrol in them that also had wheels attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were told that the Serbian soldiers pushed that down the hill and that it did not explode?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who lived there, who probably live there today, said that when you push that from the top down the hill, when the soldiers pushed that down the hill it made a very loud noise, breaking the branches and the small trees on its way down, that they could hear when this happened and that mostly then they would escape from there, because they were expecting it to explode. I don't know why it didn't explode. Probably because the people who made the device were not doing a good job. I don't know. But in any case, we did have a number of these things that did explode and that inflicted a lot of material damage. I don't know why the barrels didn't explode in that particular case. These gas cylinders for which it was established later that they were full of explosives, we don't know why they didn't explode.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This forest that you marked, it didn't exist then, but in the meantime it has grown.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a forest or a wood. These are just small shrubs, small greenery. I know after the war how high this growth is, how it was cut, what it was like before, because you can see the Sirokaca cemetery here. It was all located in a wood which had been completely cut down during the war, but now, 17 years later, it looks completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, don't you see that these trees below the arrows are higher than these buildings? And I am saying once again you were deceived, Mr. Djozo. Why would a sophisticated army that is accused here of being very capable would make these devices using old barrels? What would be the purpose of that? Who would believe you? Who would believe something like that, Mr. Djozo? Are you able to say that there is a possibility that these people deceived you, and if not, are you able to direct us to some kind of evidence? Or perhaps we can ask the Trial Chamber that we get this photograph of this device so that the witness can confirm that that is really that device. Were you deceived, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that anybody deceived me if I saw that with my very own eyes and put down in an official note exactly what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A few gas cylinders and a few barrels that didn't explode?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're not arguing with the witness at this moment. You are cross-examining the witness. Just -- just ask one question at a time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I ask that the photograph that this witness looked at and was shown by the OTP, can we look at that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then in the meantime can you please date and initial this photograph. I am asserting in the form of a question that all of this fabricated and none of it is true and that you were deceived. I cannot say that you are deceiving us here, but you were deceived there if they told you that, because that operation is quite impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Another unnecessary and unhelpful statement on your part, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The photograph that Dr. Karadzic has requested is 65 ter number 23017, and it was listed in our original notification for this witness on 22 October 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. This photo marked by the witness will be admitted as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With the number D914, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D2585, please. That is that photograph. And then can we look at page 10 in that document. Page 10 in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you confirm this photograph, Mr. Djozo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not that photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get some help so that we can see what was identified as this alleged device.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton identified it as 65 ter number 23017. We do not have it in the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's being released immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. It's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the photograph for which you stated showed an improvised device from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This kind of device I did see in that area which I marked in the previous photograph. I marked the place where these barrels were, barrels attached to wheels as is shown here. And I saw similar devices in that area just below Osmice. The only difference is that they were not barrels but gas cylinders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And here are the wheels attached to this barrel, or are they just arranged next to one another?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who photographed, the technician, and I can see the signature of the person who is a professional explosives expert, I could see that he photographed the barrel and the wheels, and you can see that there is a distance, a space between the wheels. Probably there is a barrel placed between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is this photo an identical one which is shown on the next page? Can you show the witness the next page. The lower part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, it's the -- the photograph is identical. What is it here that you see that is unusual, except that you see a barrel and wheels arranged next to each other, taken off from the vehicle in the above photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now scroll down so that we can look at the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: MR. Djozo, do you see that this is a depot of old broken-down cars and that the vehicles here are without wheels?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here are armoured personnel carriers. On the right-hand side I also see a military vehicle. It's not clear to me on the picture. I'm not able to see the barrels that are shown below. I don't know if the photograph shows the same location. The person who made these photographs, who did this photo documentation, is the only person who can know where the photographs were taken. It's not the same place as the place where I am saying I saw these barrels and gas cylinders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was photographed in the Ilijas ironworks. Mr. Djozo, are you saying that wheels are attached to these wheels, and do the barrels contain explosives, and are you saying that there was explosive placed in the gas cylinders and in the barrels that you saw below Trebevic? Are you saying that this is so? Do you have evidence to prove that this is so, or are we just supposed to take your word for it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photographs were made by the person who signed the photographs, and he probably stated that there were explosives inside. He's the only one who can say that this was so. I am saying that what I saw up there, and I put that in my report which I signed, this is a person -- this other person is the person who looked to see what was in the barrels, so he knows. I know that there were stories circulating among people in the police that the barrels contained explosives, and that in one case in the Sirokaca sector, the barrel did get through, that it did hit a house, that it caused a lot of damage. I don't know if there were any dead as a consequence. I know that they said that the explosion was quite horrendous and that it had a very negative effect on the people who were very afraid of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, both pages, on the top right corner, appear -- say page 1, and the ERN number or the eight-digit number don't seem to be contiguous. Could you help us with -- as to the origin of this photo and how come it is so?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If you could just pull back for a second so I could see the first page. I have an idea where the photo comes from -- or the photos come from, and I suspect they were drawn from a larger criminal investigation file prepared by the Bosnian police forces following the reintegration. They may have been drawn from two files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but the first page also says in English "Page 1."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Unfortunately at this moment I can't assist you on that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can assist us at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, can we then conclude that other than you hearing stories and other than seeing some gas cylinders and barrels whose contents you did not check, you don't have any proof about this explosion or about the existence of devices of this kind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have this photograph which shows what I described as seeing and wrote an official note about it, and if the Ministry of the Interior began an investigation and investigated the claim that there was explosives in the barrels, then those findings would indicate that really there was explosives in the barrels and that they were used in order to destroy both people and settlements, buildings, houses, in the area of the Stari Grad municipality, particularly in Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We're going to wait for those investigations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm intervening too much, but, Ms. Edgerton, it is only now that I realise that Ekrem Suljevic gave testimony here, but was this not put to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There wasn't enough time to cross-examine Ekrem Suljevic, but these photographs were not provided with that witness. They were provided with another witness, Miokovic or somebody else. So there were there was no opportunity to put questions about this to Suljevic. But in any case, the Defence asserts that this is just an old tyres depot and that this is not any kind of explosive device. This came with Bogdan Vidovic, with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please refrain from making statements. You are now cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I may. If I can correct myself, Your Honour. These -- this evidence was raised with Mr. Suljevic, and it appears in the transcript at pages 6174 to 6175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the Defence or by the Prosecution? You have a crib paper from Mr. Reid.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indicating the disclosure date of these photographs as 10 July 2009 for Mr. Suljevic. And this was raised with Mr. Suljevic by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, let's move on to Markale II. You are one of the people who assisted the casualties outside Markale II. Did you participate in giving first aid to the victims?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer with a yes or no. I was not there when the explosion happened. I was having breakfast in the cafeteria of the police building. We all heard the explosion, and when we got there, we asked our -- when we got back to the office, we asked our shift leader what it was about. He said it was a terrible explosion. A shell exploded outside the shopping centre. Chaos is reigning there. We tried to pass through Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street to get to the shopping centre. However, the chaos was too great. Cars were honking, people were running to and fro, crying. We couldn't get through. We returned, a group of us policemen and inspectors, because we were expecting a summons to donate blood, and that's the only assistance I was able to give in this first stage. Later on, I did not participate in the on-site investigation. I did subsequently take statements from one or two people who were wounded outside the shopping centre, but since that particular neighbourhood is covered by police station Centar, the on-site investigation was carried out by the CSB staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, I don't have much time. I'll ask you several simple questions. Did you go to Markale II at all at the time of the evacuation of the casualties?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there outside the shopping centre where the explosion occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But your statement says you heard the explosion. How many explosions did you hear?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard one horrendous explosion. I knew because of the detonation and the way the -- it sounded that the shell fell on a hard surface. Somebody who hasn't heard the explosion of a shell cannot really understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, what is your connection with Markale II? At what point and in what capacity did you get involved, apart from seeing media reports on television? What did you personally see, and what is your involvement with Markale II?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that we had set off from the station to try to help. We did not get through, so we returned to the police station because it was too crowded. There were too many cars, people running away in one direction, other people running in the opposite direction to see if they can help someone. Several days passed from that day until the time when I took a few statements from some people who were hurt in the incident. I think I took a statement from a lady who was working in a shop across the street who was wounded. I can't remember her name, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did your police station secure the scene, and which of your police officers did it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shell fell in the border area between the territories of two police stations, ours and the police station Centar. So it was mostly handled by the police station Centar. Maybe a few officers from Stari Grad joined them, but from what I know, none of my colleagues from the department was immediately involved in the on-site investigation or securing the scene. I was certainly not. I don't think any of my work colleagues were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you got to the scene, did the police from Centar -- had the police from Centar already arrived, and did you see any cameramen from Television Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not even get there. I started to go and then returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you cannot really testify about Markale II.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's my decision. I can give evidence about the things I've seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that's what you've told us today.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on your question. I looked at the footage, and I think I gave a statement saying what we heard from the SRNA agency, namely, that we had shelled ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you investigate an incident on the flea market on the 22nd December 1994?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the report, but I remember the incident. I was a member of that team. There were many people on the scene, the investigating judge and all the other members of the team. I went there to help out my colleague who was on duty that day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have to call that document. It was probably admitted through another witness. Can we get 1D2768 so you can mark these locations. Can we zoom in on the right-hand half.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark, Mr. Djozo, the place where your station is located and the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Lugavina Street, and I see the letter P for "Parking lot."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take the pen and please help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just to note that the very first exhibit was Mr. Djozo marking the location of his police station on a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but -- but we need to find that one to familiarise ourselves in this map. So let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the site of the incident at the flea market.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the name of that street. Where is it? Is it near Oprkanj? That's the area where the flea market was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's your area.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The streets have been renamed, and it's very hard to do that. The flea market continues into this area. It begins at the parking lot in Bravadziluk upwards, and it's in this street that people organise the flea market. It is called flea market, because people sold anything that could sell, thread, needles, cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put the date and your initials. Number 2 is the flea market, a site of an incident.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D915, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You have five minutes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time this happened, the incident and the investigation?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. It was too long ago, 18 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How soon after the incident did you come to the scene?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that either, but we would normally come out to the scene within 30 minutes, an hour, two hours after the incident. It all depended on the shelling. Sometimes we couldn't go at all because of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you find at the scene? Was it at least two or three hours before you were able to come?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, when we got there we did not find any wounded people there anymore. I know that I didn't see any wounded when I arrived. I know that we looked for fragments of the shell. I know that it turned out it was probably not a mortar, because the shrapnel seemed to belong to another weapon, and I seem to remember that people were saying it was some kind of mountain gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You didn't see any casualties, but two people are said to have been killed.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking of the dead, I cannot say off-the-cuff, but if the record says and the statements from the hospital and from the witnesses say so, then it is so, because usually after a shell explodes, the people who are nearby try to take the wounded to the hospital as soon as possible to try to save them. And if somebody was killed on the spot, if it says so in the report, it must be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you don't know. Do you know who evacuated these alleged wounded and the alleged dead? Is it the case that it was not only the police but also members of the BH Army who came to their assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic mentioned the names of some witnesses who made that claim. The interpreter didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters couldn't catch some of the names you referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned the name of Salih Djedovic. It's a witness whose statement I believe is in evidence, and he stated that members of the police and members of the BH Army came to the rescue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you arrived together with the investigating team, and you found no bodies at all, none wounded or dead. You confirmed that today. Was there a single investigation where you found the wounded and the dead still on site?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an impossibility, because when something like that happens, that is to say, in these cases after shellings where people were killed and wounded, the police station would be informed. And since I worked in my department, I was not one of the field operatives waiting for a shell to fall to help the casualties. I was working in my office, and I would be informed by the shift leader from the uniformed police who would tell me about the incident, and then we would begin to form an investigation team. That can take a while, as I said before. It all depends on whether the investigating judge is able to come immediately. If they are not too busy with other investigations in other locations, it can take them 15 minutes, 30 minutes, an hour. However, if the shelling is too strong, if the investigation team is already out there investigating in the field, then it can take longer. It never happened that I just happened to be somewhere where something happened and was able to give assistance to the casualties. People who were wounded were immediately transported by survivors to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have any proof that 10.000 civilians were killed in Sarajevo and 1.300 children, or are you just repeating something you heard from others?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These things are very serious, and we should not joke about this or mock such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which major incident -- incidents did these 10.000 civilians get killed? Where did these incidents happen?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire territory of the city of Sarajevo, from the very beginning, from 1992 until 1995, was shelled every day, especially the area of Stari Grad, the Old Town. I think it's obvious from all the films and interviews with people. The town hall burnt down immediately, and houses in Stari Grad. People were getting killed on every corner. You were not safe even in an air shelter, because the VRS had such an arsenal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, this is the last question I'm allowed. I'm asking you as a witness, as an investigator and a police officer, to enumerate major incidents in which during 1260 days of war, 10.000 civilians and 1.300 children got killed. What are these incidents, and where are we to find proof?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proof is available to everyone, especially to this Honourable Court and the Prosecution, so there's no need for me to enumerate, but from the town hall to Stup, Ilidza, Novi Grad, Dobrinja, Sirokaca, Sedrenik, Kosevo, there is not a single spot, not a single street where people didn't die, in streetcars, in their own cars, waiting for water near the Sarajevo brewery. There is not a single street, not a house, not a building where somebody did not get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's turn it this way: There are two major incidents, Markale I and Markale II. Is there a third major incident?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There is the marketplace. There is the incident where children got killed near the secondary school. There is Alipasino Polje. There are people in Dobrinja who got killed, if I remember well, during a cease-fire. People were playing ball and then somebody from Republika Srpska got bored, I suppose, and threw bombs on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's sufficient. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, earlier on today in the transcript Dr. Karadzic asked you the following. He said: "You are unable to give us the names of those who were killed in the Sedrenik settlement, or are you?" And your response was: "The lists exist. They are available. You can see exactly how many people in total, how many women, how many elderly, and how many children were killed." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you now a document that I have, because it's a large document, available beside me in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And for the record, it's 65 ter number 23068, and I could ask my colleague to deliver this copy to the witness. It might be easier for him. While we can view e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djozo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does the Defence want to look at the document before the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
